title: NudgeRatchet's failure-mode enumeration omits NudgeStreamer__ZeroReceived, and diverges silently from BalancerPoolerV2's failure semantics
priorTitle: RETIRED 2026-07-30: 'Cross-contract failure-isolation asymmetry: a streamer revert bricks the mint, not just the flush'. The prior title asserted the AVAILABILITY FOOTGUN LIMB THAT THIS RUN ITSELF REFUTED (see law3Verdict). Standing alone that limb is a reckless-admin invalid, and a finding whose title claims the limb its own analysis kills will be scored on the title. RESCOPED to lead on the residual; the availability mechanism is retained as FLAGGED CONTEXT (documented, deliberate) and is explicitly NOT the claim.
description: NudgeRatchet.dispatch calls collectNudge bare. A revert there bricks the MINT itself (NudgeRatchet.dispatch -> NFTMinterV2._executeMint -> mint) for every minter on that dispatcher, batched or single - not merely the flush. BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch wraps the SAME hop to the SAME contract in an explicit, documented, story-047-mandated try/catch envelope ('streamer unset, stream not registered' named among the swallowed reverts); NudgeRatchet leaves it bare. Story-031 widened the un-isolated leg's revert surface by adding NudgeStreamer__ZeroReceived at :199.
impact: Availability. Wider blast radius than L-01 (every mint on that dispatcher). Fails CLOSED and is one-owner-transaction recoverable (registerStream). Donor funds keep accumulating safely in the streamer buffer and flush normally afterwards. No value lost - nudge delivery is delayed, not destroyed; users lose reverted-transaction gas only.
law3Verdict: NOT A SURPRISE => not a footgun on the primary limb. NudgeRatchet's own contract NatSpec (lib/yield-claim-nft @ d4cc563, :23-43) discloses the ENTIRE hazard accurately and in advance: it names the exact revert (NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered()), states the blast radius ('every dispatch'), covers the setBatchMinter REPOINT case, and prescribes a numbered required ops ordering with setNudgeStreamer explicitly LAST. An owner performing this wiring is following a runbook, not walking into a surprise. NOT DEFERENCE TO THE 'NOT an audit finding' CLAUSE: per standing policy in-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority, and that sentence carries none here. What does the work is the SURROUNDING DISCLOSURE BEING ACCURATE AND COMPLETE, verified against the code rather than taken on trust. The MEMORY rule that RAISES severity applies to FALSELY-exhaustive documentation; this documentation is true.
rescopedBasis: THE FINDING IS THE RESIDUAL, NOT THE BRICK. Limb 1 (SUBSTANTIVE, confirmed at source at 9611312 / yield-claim-nft d4cc563): NudgeStreamer declares NudgeStreamer__ZeroReceived() at :93 and reverts it at :199; NudgeRatchet's failure-mode enumeration at :29-38 lists `nudgeStreamer unset`, NotRegistered, NotWhitelisted and ZeroAmount, and ZeroReceived APPEARS NOWHERE IN NudgeRatchet (grep over the file: zero hits). story-031 widened the un-isolated leg's revert surface without updating an otherwise-complete enumeration. Present-tense, demonstrated, AND NOT AN OWNER ACTION AT ALL - which is exactly why it survives the reckless-admin rule that disposes of the availability framing. Limb 2 (SUPPORTING, WEAKER - do not lead on it): cross-contract failure-semantics divergence; one streamer, two dispatchers, opposite outcomes for the identical condition, with BalancerPoolerV2's NatSpec training the reader that 'a streamer misconfiguration is quiet'. Partly self-defeating, because the operator wiring NudgeRatchet reads NudgeRatchet's NatSpec, which is accurate and ordering-prescriptive.
flaggedContextNotClaim: The mint blast radius is RETAINED AS CONTEXT and must be presented as documented and deliberate: NudgeRatchet.dispatch calls collectNudge bare, so a revert bricks the MINT (dispatch -> NFTMinterV2._executeMint -> mint) for every minter on that dispatcher; the hop is un-isolated ON PURPOSE (story-046 removed the direct-transfer fallback deliberately, no donation-disable switch). It fails CLOSED, is one-owner-transaction recoverable (registerStream), loses no value. DO NOT re-lead on this limb.
doesNotFollowL01OnIssuerEvent: L-03 does NOT follow L-01 to Medium on the USDC-pause / USDT-blocklist vector, and fails the incremental test HARDER. NudgeRatchet's prime token is USDC (constructor-enforced 6 decimals) and the mint payment arrives on the dispatcher in that same USDC via NFTMinterV2._executeMint's safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, config.dispatcher, price). Under a GLOBAL USDC PAUSE THE MINT IS ALREADY BRICKED AT THE PAYMENT LEG, before dispatch is reached => ZERO INCREMENTAL IMPACT from the un-isolated hop. Only a TARGETED blocklist of the batchMinter is incremental, and recovery is messier than L-01's (no donation-disable switch by design, so escape means repointing batchMinter and registering the new pair - two-plus owner txs, stranding the old buffer). Messier, but still recoverable, still loud, still not attacker-inducible.
survivingResidual: The ONE substantive gap: NudgeRatchet's failure-mode enumeration at :29-38 lists `nudgeStreamer unset`, NotRegistered, NotWhitelisted and ZeroAmount, and OMITS NudgeStreamer__ZeroReceived - so story-031 widened the revert surface of the un-isolated leg without updating an otherwise-complete list. Plus a cross-contract INCONSISTENCY OF FAILURE SEMANTICS: one streamer, two dispatchers, opposite outcomes for the identical condition, and BalancerPoolerV2's own NatSpec trains the reader in the OTHER direction ('a streamer misconfiguration is quiet'). An operator carrying that model to NudgeRatchet is wrong.
severityNote: Low UPHELD by the severity-classifier against a Medium dissent; the dissent's central premise was REFUTED, not merely outweighed. C4 Medium availability discriminators all point Low: NOT attacker-inducible (requires a privileged config action), does NOT arise in normal operation without operator error, NOT silent (self-naming custom error on the very first mint attempt, atomically), NOT unrecoverable (one owner registerStream transaction), NO value lost. Medium availability findings need the outage to be attacker-inducible, OR undetectable, OR unrecoverable; this is none of the three.
escalationTriggers: A path is found where collectNudge reverts WITHOUT a privileged action - in particular a plain-ERC20 counterexample to INV-1 (sum(buffer_i) <= balanceOf(streamer)) with >= 3 STREAMS ON ONE TOKEN, which symbolic-results.json records as INCONCLUSIVE-TIMEOUT at wide bounds (PASS only below 2^32), resting on one HAND-CHECKED reduction step. That would make _settle's transfer revert in NORMAL OPERATION, and the outage would arrive unannounced instead of at bring-up. => MEDIUM.
NudgeStreamer acquires a pause, deregistration, or duration-zeroing path, making the brick reachable from a routine live operation. => MEDIUM.

Any dispatcher acquires a collectNudge hop NOT covered by an accurate, ordering-prescribing disclosure of this failure mode. *** CORRECTED 2026-07-30 (remediation pass): => RE-WEIGH, WITH THE FOOTGUN LIMB NO LONGER MITIGATED - NOT '=> MEDIUM'. *** The prior wording ('the disclosure is what holds this at Low, and IT IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE CODE') OVER-STATED what documentation can do. Accurate documentation moves the SURPRISE/LIKELIHOOD limb ONLY; it cannot move impact, detectability or recoverability - and those ARE code properties that hold this finding at Low/QA on their own (not attacker-inducible, self-naming atomic revert on the first mint attempt, one-transaction recoverable, no value lost). Deleting the NatSpec would make this an UNDOCUMENTED footgun with a loud, atomic, one-tx-recoverable failure at bring-up - still Low/QA. A watch that promises a Medium it cannot deliver gets discounted the first time it fires.

remediationReversal.withdrawn: The proposed disposition's cross-repo obligation to 'cross-file the missing try/catch to the yield-claim-nft ledger' is WITHDRAWN. DO NOT FILE 'wrap collectNudge in try/catch' AS THE MITIGATION. This is the run's most important output.
remediationReversal.reason1: IT CONVERTS A LOUD FAILURE INTO A SILENT ONE. ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch (:124-125) executes _dispatch(...) THEN hook.onDispatch(minter, amount, extraData). A swallowed collectNudge therefore lets _dispatch return successfully: the USDC stays on the dispatcher while the hook accrues mint-debt against `amount`, and nothing surfaces. This is a TRANSIENT backing/debt timing skew - self-healing, because _dispatch sweeps the whole balance (`bal`) on the next dispatch, so no permanent over-accrual occurs and NO unbacked-phUSD claim is filed. But it is precisely the direction NudgeRatchet:148-149 guards against, and it sits adjacent to the tracked DEDUP-001 unbacked-phUSD class in yield-claim-nft.
remediationReversal.reason2: SILENCE IS THE AGGRAVATOR THIS AUDIT PENALISES ELSEWHERE. L-05 (D-26-08) is filed specifically for a SILENT streamer misconfiguration, and BalancerPoolerV2's NatSpec itself warns that its try/catch makes streamer misconfiguration QUIET. Adding a catch here trades a self-diagnosing, one-transaction-recoverable revert for a quiet, indefinitely-accumulating misconfiguration - moving NudgeRatchet INTO the L-05 failure class to escape a Low.
remediationReversal.alsoContradicts: A deliberate, documented design decision: story-046 removed the direct-transfer fallback ON PURPOSE and there is no donation-disable switch.

recommendation: *** THE REBAND TO QA DOES NOT SOFTEN THE MITIGATION TRAP: 'DO NOT wrap collectNudge in try/catch' IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE REASON THE REBAND IS SAFE. See remediationReversal. *** Documentation and consistency, matching the honest severity. (1) Add the missing NudgeStreamer__ZeroReceived row to NudgeRatchet's failure-mode enumeration at :29-38 (the one substantive gap). (2) Document the DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from BalancerPoolerV2: state at ALL THREE sites (NudgeRatchet, BalancerPoolerV2, and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer:293-296 on the phoenix side - see watch2604Correction.thirdMitigationSite) why one dispatcher fails closed on a streamer fault and the other fails open, so an operator cannot carry the wrong model between them. (3) KEEP THE REVERT - it is the correct, deliberate, story-046 behaviour. The cross-file to yield-claim-nft still happens, but as a DOCUMENTATION-CONSISTENCY item against NudgeRatchet:29-38, not as a missing-guard item.
